semantic_candidates.evidence: A radius-10 cylinder is swept through 3*pi/2 radians over 25 millimetres and closed by two sector caps and two radial planes.

validation_findings.evidence: The two radius-10 cap arcs span 3*pi/2 and every axial or radial closure line has positive length.
Two exact circle arcs and seven exact line segments account for every unique edge.
The retained U interval is 3*pi/2 rather than a full period, so its two longitudinal boundaries are distinct and no seam edge is identified.
The no-processing STEP round trip records 1e-7 millimetres, equal to 1e-10 metres, for every vertex, edge, and face tolerance.
The lateral patch, two cap sectors, and two radial closures pair all nine unique boundary edges.
Each of the nine unique edges has exactly two face uses in one connected closed component.
V-E+F equals 6-9+5=2 and the 3*pi/2 sweep is strictly between zero and a full period.

oracle.statement: A 3*pi/2 cylindrical sector has one cylindrical patch, two planar sector caps, and two radial closure planes. The two circular arcs, two outer axial lines, four radial cap lines, and one shared axis line give nine edges and six vertices; paired face uses yield eighteen edge and thirty-six endpoint occurrences.
